correctness.rationale: For distinct matrix units both nonzero products cannot coincide, so commuting is exactly the simultaneous mismatch of the two middle indices. Inclusion–exclusion and loop removal give the stated adjacency operator. On symmetric arrays, diagonal and row-sum data together separate the constant and zero-sum sectors: the (I,J) data map has determinant n−1 up to sign and the (D_u,P_u) data map determinant n−2 up to sign. The remaining symmetric kernel has dimension n(n−3)/2 since the unsigned complete-graph incidence has full row rank (a_i+a_j=0 for every i≠j forces a=0 for n≥3). Skew row sums are onto 1-perp via Q_u, leaving the stated −2 space. The resulting determinants reproduce all factors; the quadratics have no common root (their difference forces λ=(n−2)/(n−1), which leaves λ² in the second quadratic), and the listed linear eigenvalues do not collide with them. Only the nullity factor vanishes at zero. The positive-root sum and mixed-sign root difference, with the linear contributions, give the stated energy.
residual_risks: Independent checks at n=3,…,7 test exact finite polynomials, not the quantified direct-sum proof. The n=2 degeneracy is excluded.
